location: Bergmansparken, Arboga, Arboga/Stockholm, Sweden
description: Welcome to Arboga Medieval Days! This is a weekend where Arboga Medieval Society invites each and all that loves medieval things to come join us. Medieval market, lectures, workshops, Knight's jousting (Arboga Knights), music and much more. Everything a good medieval weekend needs! This year the Shire of Löghammar are invited by Arboga Medieval society to join them in a medieval camping where we can show of our crafting and hold lectures and workshops. This event is not an SCA-event, it is organized by Arboga Medieval Society in the town of Arboga in Sweden and it will be open for mundanes. SCA Löghammar will be represented without our own camp but within the medieval camp as a collaboration together with Arboga Medieval society. Tents will be set up Tuesday 4/8. After Wednesday 5/8 10:00 am there will be no cars allowed in camp unless you have spoken with the event steward and made arrangements due to special needs. The camp will be open for mundanes and others to visit between 10:00 - 15:00 Wednesday - Saturday. We love people to then hand around to be able to answer questions from visitors about what we do within the SCA. description: New to the SCA and unsure how to get started? Already here but want to try something new? Or are you the type who wants to do it all? This is the event for you! Past years have included thrown weapons, scribal classes, block printing, how to get started brewing, how to repair your combat gear, and more. This year, we are welcoming back Montgomery Josh and his siege engines! Our goal is showing you creative and budget friendly ways to discover a new passion. We will keep our event Facebook page updated as we confirm teachers and add classes. To that end we are seeking teachers, come share what you wish you knew when you found the SCA. How about tips for budget friendly ways to get started or smart thrifting and repurposing of everyday items. In short, share how not to break the bank and look fabulous! To teach a class, sign up here! https://forms.gle/jjrRiDGiiTuqSGeX7 Our event is family and newcomer friendly. Eisental has planned the event to be welcoming and inclusive. To start, there is no set fee, however we are encouraging donations to help defray the cost of the site. Further, garb is encouraged, and gold key will be available but not required, making it perfect for anyone who is simply curious and wants to check things out. Join us October 30 – November 1, 2026, as we witness the Investiture of our new Baronage and mark the beginning of a new chapter in the history of our beloved Barony. Come gather beneath banners flying proudly in the crisp autumn air as Their Excellencies take up the mantle of leadership. Let voices be raised in acclamation, cups lifted in good cheer, and friendships renewed around hearth and table. The lists shall come alive with displays of valor as armored combatants contest for honor and glory, while rapier fighters test their skill and courtesy upon the field. Archers and throwers alike are invited to demonstrate their precision and prowess upon the ranges, proving that steady hands and keen eyes are as worthy as strength of arm. Those with a love of the arts and sciences are encouraged to attend in their finest attire. Let the fields and halls be adorned with elegant cotehardies, splendid kirtles, graceful hoods, and all manner of medieval finery befitting the season. Whether clad in humble wool or noble silk, all are welcome to share in the beauty and inspiration of our Society. As evening falls, gather for a sumptuous feast where good company, laughter, and excellent fare shall abound. Tales will be told, songs will be sung, and memories made to last through many winters to come. In keeping with the festive spirit of the season, all are invited to participate in our Pet Costume Contest! Bring forth your most noble hounds or any beloved (toy) companion bedecked in medieval splendor, heraldic glory, or harvest merriment. Prizes and admiration await those creatures most charmingly attired. Whether you come seeking martial renown, artistic inspiration, delicious fare, or simply the joy of gathering among friends, there shall be a place for you at our celebration. So don your finest garb , prepare your banners, and make haste to Dun Carraig. Together let us honor the past, celebrate the present, and welcome our new Baronage with all the pomp, ceremony, and merriment that such an occasion deserves. By our hands and hearts, we invite you to join us for this grand and joyous Investiture Weekend. October 30 – November 1, 2026 Vivat Atlantia! Vivat Dun Carraig! Vivat Their Excellencies!

description: Unto the Good People of Caid, warm Greetings and most gracious Salutations! The Barony of Dun Or joyfully invites one and all to join us for a day of mirth, merriment and noble fellowship at the Festival of the Rose, to be held upon Saturday, the Fifteenth of August 2026. Come and join us in a splendid celebration of love, beauty, and the Arts and Artisans of glorious Caid, held in honor of Her Royal Majesty, our radiant and most beloved Queen Fara! The noble tradition of the Festival of the Rose first blossomed in the year 1980 as the Queen’s Arts Tea, when Her Royal Majesty Amsha called upon the Chivalry and the Royal Guard to display their skill and talents in honor of the occasion, and in tribute to the Crown. In that same spirit of inspiration, Her Majesty, Queen Fara, most warmly invites and encourages all associates to the Peerage — Squires, Apprentices, Protégés, Provosts, and Prodigies alike — together with all artisans, scholars, and performers throughout the realm, to present the fruits of their skill and imagination in the Arts, Sciences, and the Bardic traditions. Whether set forth for admiration or entered in honorable competition, let all works be offered in celebration of Her Majesty and in pursuit of the title of Her Champion. And should you have need of treasures rare and wondrous, rejoice! A silent auction will be held for the benefit of the Kingdom Travel Fund! If you are interested in gifting the auction with any treasures - in good condition, of course- that you may no longer need, please bring them for inclusion, or email a detailed gift certificate to Her Royal Majesty's Chamberlain, Duchess Lorissa, at ! We look forward to celebrating Beauty, Love, and Our Beloved Queen Fara with you at the Festival of the Rose! Happy feet that simply *must* dance in honor of Her Majesty? If so, you are welcome to do so during our Performance Art Presentations! description: Both Armored Combat and Rapier fighter practice are held Saturdays, 8am-10am, near Ramada #11 (SE side) of Caballero Park in Yuma, AZ. For notices of cancellation please check our calendar and our Facebook group! If you are interested in combat sports and martial arts, come give it a try! We have loaner gear available, just let us know you are interested by emailing our marshal at .org or posting to our Facebook group! Note you will want to bring your own hard-shelled sports cup (groin protection namely for males) and maybe wear long sleeved clothing. Otherwise, we have everything else you need, you just have to show up! You must be 16 and older to participate and must sign a waiver for liability purposes at every practice unless you are a paid member and authorized to fight in the SCA. Participants under 18 years old must have a parent or legal guardian present to sign a waiver and consent form. What to expect your first time at a fighter practice: We will go over all safety requirements and procedures before having you (or your parent/legal guardian) sign a waiver. Then we will help you get armored up from our loaners appropriate for armored combat or rapier, depending on your expressed interest. We then will do an armor inspection to make sure your armor meets minimum requirements and is safe. Next, we will help calibrate, which involves delivering a blow to your person to help you understand the varying degrees of force used, i.e. what is considered light, good, and excessive. We will go over some basic rules including what striking areas are legal or not. Next, we will go over and practice some basic stances and techniques to make sure you can safely deliver a blow and defend yourself. Finally, we let you have a go at it and see what you can do! Many first timers struggle with having an idea in there head of what is going to happen and executing that idea the way they pictured it. More often than not it almost never works out the way you imagined it, and that is okay! That shouldn’t discourage you from trying something that sounds cool in your head, sometimes it works out and can surprise even the most seasoned of fighters! We are all students and teachers here, even you, and we learn the most when we humble ourselves to those facts. For more information on safety and rules, please refer to the SCA Armored Combat (Rattan) Marshals Handbook and/or Atenveldt Rapier Handbook found in the Kingdom Document Library [RECURRING — also on: 4 Jul 2026, 11 Jul 2026, 18 Jul 2026, 25 Jul 2026, 1 Aug 2026, 8 Aug 2026, 15 Aug 2026, 22 Aug 2026]

title: Gyldenholt Anniversary
location: Cedar Grove Park, 11385 Pioneer Rd, Tustin, CA 92782, USA
description: By invitation of their Excellencies Baron Brynjólfr Brandsson and Baroness Dyrfinna Drengsdottir of Gyldenholt, we bid ye gather with us when the sun reaches its zenith and the days stretch long over our golden groves for this grand day where the flames of the forge meet the fire of the soul at the Tournament of the Sun: A Festival of Fire and Spice . Gather round, ye fighters of flame and artisans of pungent root. A call to glory rings out, bidding the bold to bring forth their finest, for the fervor of competition beckons. Their Excellencies will seek Champions in the following categories: Combat: Armored, Rapier, Cut & Thrust, and Youth Champions Arts & Sciences: The Barony of Gyldenholt Annual Arts & Sciences Champion Bardic: The Barony of Gyldenholt Annual Bardic Champion Awards: The Motley Mêlée Theatre: Best Fiery Performance The Paramour of Picante: Spiciest Complement on the Tourney Field Best Use of Spices & Herbs in an Arts & Sciences Entry: All Categories Welcome As we are blithe on this day to celebrate all periods from Greek to Norse to Ottoman to Tudor, we bid you dress in your finest fiery attire of sun gold, bold crimson, and delicious saffron. “I hope for dear summertime; wait - be willing in favour of me; smile, love, smile.” ~ Inscription on a 15th Century Saddle SCHEDULE: 8am: Site Open 10:00am: Opening Court - at Their Majesty’s pleasure Lists close 15 minutes after the end of Opening Court - fighting will start shortly thereafter 11:30am: Arts & Sciences competition drop-off period ends & populace voting begins Children’s Activities Will Be Between Rounds 12pm – 1pm: Bardic Competition under the Baronial Pavilion- fighters can arrange time with Their Excellencies, as needed 1pm – 2pm: Artisan Showcase under the Arts Ramada 2pm - 3pm: Theatrical Scene Performances under the Baronial Pavilion 4pm: Closing Court - approximate time depending on combat finals 6pm: Site closes ARTS & SCIENCES COMPETITION for the Baronial Arts & Sciences Champion . The entries do not need to adhere to the theme of the day but it is appreciated if they do. Entries should be displayed under the Arts Ramada by 11:30am. BARDIC COMPETITION for the Baronial Bardic Champion . The bardic pieces do not need to adhere to the theme of the day, but it is appreciated if they do. Due to allotted time, we ask that the bardic pieces be no more than 3 minutes in length. COMBAT SCENARIOS: For Rapier and Armored Combatants: This year, your challenge shall be… spiciest compliment on the tourney field to win the Paramour of Picante Award ! In honor of the theme of the day, Tournament of the Sun: A Festival of Fire and Spice , a special benefit will be given to those on the tourney field when offering a compliment to an esteemed opponent. Have your flattery and wit at the ready! - Scenario: Single Elimination, 1 Spicy Complement = 1 Extra Life Bonus - Spicy Compliment Bonus: 1 Per Tournament IMPORTANT: In order to earn the Extra Life Bonus, you must issue your compliment *prior* to exiting the field following a loss. After the bonus is received, compliments may be administered liberally at thine discretion for the remainder of the tournament. Youth Combat is scheduled to begin after the 4th round of Armored Fighting. A Youth Champion will be chosen based on the most honorable and chivalrous combatant. ACTIVITIES: The Motley Mêlée Theater Award: Time limit: 2 minutes for 1 performer, 3 minutes for 2 performers, and a max of 5 minutes for 3 or more performers. Performances must be PG rated and suitable to a family audience. To be performed in the Baronial Pavillion. It is not a requirement that these scenes be drawn from period pieces but more inspired by medieval life. Shakespeare is always welcome but you may draw from modern pieces, dramatic and humorous, such as Elizabeth, The Merchant of Venice, Men In Tights, The Court Jester, Monty Python, The Princess Bride, etc. We only ask you to stick to the theme of the day, Tournament of the Sun: A Festival of Fire and Spice . The award will be for Best Fiery Performance . Best Use of an Herb or Spice Award: All categories are welcome! Baroness Dyrfinna challenges the populace to have fun and play with our theme of the day by incorporating the spirit of herbs and spices into your dress, decor, or feast table for the day. If you’ve “cooked” up something special, please bring it to Her Excellency’s attention as she makes her progress. As Her Excellency will be selecting the winner, please refrain from using ginger or jasmine in any submission due to allergy . Herbal Craft Activity: Our Baroness Dyrfinna graciously invites the populace to join her for a craft activity of card making with elements of period spices, plants, and flowers. Please join us under the Arts Ramada for this lovely activity, children are most welcome! Arts & Sciences Competition and Display: Please set up your item(s) for display at one of the tables under the Arts Ramada by 11:30am. We will have a 1 hour artisan showcase from 1pm to 2pm. All artisans are asked to participate by coming to the Arts Pavilion and stand with their art and discuss. Arts entries can also include what you are wearing for the day or heraldic/decorative display at your pavilion, if it fits the theme, Tournament of the Sun: A Festival of Fire and Spice . If this is the case for your entry, please provide a paper with at least your name, a description of your entry (and ideally a photo of said entry) at the display table during the competition and, if possible, be present for the artisan showcase. Please note, Arts & Sciences entries do not need to follow the theme of the day. The entries do not require documentation, but it is encouraged. MERCHANTS: Merchants are welcome however, you must provide for your own city license and insurance. Please contact the Stewards in advance to let us know you are coming. EVENT REGISTRATION: Adult Event Registration: $25. Adult Member Discount Event Registration: $15. Children 17 and under are guests of the Barony. Cash and checks accepted at the gate. Please make checks payable to “SCA Inc./Barony of Gyldenholt”. Please Note: This is a dry site. PARKING: Parking at the park is limited, please unload and then park at Pioneer Middle School. description: Muse's Masque is Caid's newest arts event coming up on August 29th. The event is not selling any tickets at the door and is pre-register only. Both standard tickets ($50 member, $60 non-member) and a more limited number of patron’s tickets ($100/$110) are available. Those patron’s tickets will include a special upgraded site token and your name and arms on a Patron’s Roll of Arms. The event includes food in its ticket cost and the venue is selling alcohol on site. There will also be baubling, live music, dancing and a fashion show. For more information, or to purchase tickets go to: caid/muses-masque-2/ Patron Registration closes July 16 at 10 PM. Standard Registration closes August 21 at 10 PM. We have a variety of classes and workshops that are feeding into this event over the course of the next year, leading up to August 29, 2026. Keep an eye out for many other upcoming opportunities to learn dance, play music, and get help with costuming. Site The beautiful site has plentiful parking. Join us in the Banquet Hall of the David L. Baker Golf Course. They have a rock solid air conditioning system. Food and Beverages Your admission to the Masque includes an assortment of period party foods made by a collection of Caid's fabulous chefs. The meal is being presented as a series of social small plates, rather than a sit-down feast. While dessert is included in the cost of your ticket, we’re also setting up a bonus potluck dessert area for additional sweets. The venue is managing an on-site bar where alcohol will be available for purchase. Baubling There will be a parlor with games of skill and chance. There will be opportunities to wager your baubles in good-natured gambling. We will be offering several bags of notable and special baubles for sale for $5 a bag at the event. (Those that have small items of interest, be they unique tokens from SCA experiences or well loved and traveled baubles from the gaming community, and would like to donate to this cause, please speak to His Excellency Diego de Palma, mka Benjamin Dean Doggett.) Free bauble bags will be available as well for those that wish to start their collection and start playing at games. The silent auction will close at approximately 8:30 pm. Only PayPal payments will be accepted for silent auction items. Dancing and Music You can expect plenty of dancing at the Masque and live music as well. description: EN/FI/SWE Rajataverna - Gränstavernan 30.7-2.8.2026 Again, the northern medieval and Iron Age folk will gather on the border and welcome all travelers from near and far! This will be the first time the Tavern will be located in Finland. The site is a hunting lodge 10 km from the Swedish border. The event will be a relaxed reenactment event, which is open to new and old historical reenactors. The event is organized by the Peräpohjolan keskiaikaseura which is part of the international Society for Creative Anachronism and Suomen keskiaikaseura (The medieval society of Finland). In the terms of the Society: The village of Torna in Aarnimetsä, Drachenwald. We are even collaborating with Frostheim (Luleå) from the principality of Nordmark (Sweden) and are officially sponsored by Kaarnemaa (Oulu) from Aarnimetsä. Although Rajataverna / Gräsntavernan is a SCA-event, you do not need to be a member of the society in order to participate! Rajataverna is a place for everyone to meet regardless of any borders. The event languages are Finnish, Swedish and English. The program is currently under construction and we are looking for teachers in Arts & Sciences, fighting, etc. If you want to teach, let us know! There will be a homely feast and a small market, where you can bring new and second hand items. The program is updating all the time and the final schedule will be published well before the event. It is possible to arrive at the site on Friday 17 o’clock and the event site must be empty by midday on Sunday. Please note that Rajataverna is living in Finnish time due to its location. The hunting lodge Tapiolan maja has cabins for 24 persons. You are free to bring your own tent and we will create a crash space if needed. The lodge has a sauna and a fireplace. Whole weekend (includes accommodation & food) 40 € / 440 kr SCA-members 45 € / 470 kr non-members 20 € / 210 kr minors Children under 7 are free Day visit on Saturday (includes food) 15 € / 170 kr for an adult 10 € / 110 kr children over 7 years The meals include snacks on Friday evening, breakfast, lunch and feast on Saturday and breakfast on Sunday. People coming from outside the Nordics can pay at the door. Payment information will be sent later via email. title: Siege of the City
location: City of Rocks State Park, 327 NM-61, Faywood, New Mexico, 88034
description: A Halloween Siege for warriors of all ages! Darkness gathers at the Siege of the City! Join the Shire of Nahrun Kabirun for Halloween battles, costumes, and chilling festivities. As the veil thins and mischief stirs among the ancient stones, the Shire of Nahrun Kabirun invites all wanderers, warriors, and wayward spirits to gather at City of Rocks for our Halloween‑season Siege of the City! Friday, as the Veil thins, bards will weave haunting tales and playful chills during our Spooky Bardic. Saturday, the rocks will ring with spooky‑themed Heavy and Rapier combat, where steel clashes and eerie laughter echoes between the formations. Archers may test their courage and aim in both the Archery Contest and Pumpkin Shoot. Young adventurers, and the young at heart, can embark on a Treasure Hunt among the stones. As twilight deepens and the rocks take on their ghostly silhouettes, we will gather for an Autumn Potluck Feast. Bring a dish to share if you are able. Trick‑or‑Treating for ALL ages will commence after the Autumn Potluck. Donations of treats are warmly welcomed to help spread the magic and mischief throughout the evening. Enjoy a night of dancing, games, and fellowship. Music will rise until quiet hours at 10 p.m., after which soft drumming and gentle melodies may linger like friendly spirits in the dark. Join us for a weekend where whimsy meets wonder, where battles and bardic tales mingle with pumpkins and starlight, and where the spirit of the Siege awakens beneath the watchful stones. Gate:Adult: $30Adult Member: $20Youth (18 & below): Free Primitive Site Fees are charged per vehicle, walk‑in, or bicycle, per night by New Mexico State Parks. • New Mexico Residents: $10.00 per night• Non‑Residents: $15.00 per night These fees help support the park and keep our beautiful site available for future adventures. Thank you for planning ahead and contributing to the magic of the weekend

description: Sign Up: d/e/1FAIpQLSfpYdJ_ 3tnjeiJfWvOyTDsT6LTv- muxuz2jbKeiTrtD-LOfCg/viewform About the Event: This is our first year at Silverado Children’s Center! SCC is a nature based pre-school and daycare in the beautiful Silverado Canyon area! Our school is small but mighty, with our students in the 2-5 year age range. We have invited the community to join as well, so we do expect parents and older siblings! What we are looking for : Fighting demos for sword forms (Armored, rapier, unarmored, C&T, whatever we get folks for!) art displays, and lot and lots of hands on touchable displays and activities! Our audience is very young, so we are very interested in things that can be touched and interacted with! Anyone willing to run take-home crafting is also greatly desired! Those with experience or love with very small children are greatly welcome!! “No-touch displays” that show off blacksmithing, archery and daily life are also welcomed, but will need to be attended. Driving and parking: The center is on Santiago Canyon road, which is accessible from the 55 Freeway from the North, or the 5 Freeway south, or the 241 toll road. Our center is located behind the Library of the Canyons, and has its own driveway just north of the main library entrance. Please park in the lower lot (closer to the road.) There is NO street parking. Santiago canyon is a two lane, high speed country road! Please drive safely! If there is no parking left at SCC, you can park at the Library, walk behind it and up the hill and there we are! For more info, scheduling issues, if you get lost etc please contact Baroness Dyrfinna Phone- (texting okay!)

description: For Twelfth Night 2027, the populace is invited to celebrate a season of transition, where old traditions and joyful excess meet at the turning of the year. The theme draws inspiration from late medieval southern Germany and Switzerland, where winter observances blended seamlessly with lively seasonal celebrations marking the close of one cycle and the promise of the next. By the fifteenth century, these celebrations had fused into a distinctive blend of formality and fun. Daytime brought courtly pomp, displays of skill, and structured ceremony, while nightfall ushered in feasting, dancing, and masked revelry. This balance of order and exuberance provides the perfect setting for Atlantia’s Twelfth Night, offering a full day of pageantry and arts followed by an evening devoted to celebration, community, and unapologetic joy. During this time, the days surrounding Twelfth Night marked the end of the winter holiday season and the gradual shift toward spring. Communities gathered for pageantry, symbolic acts of renewal, and public festivities that reflected both reflection and anticipation. These moments were as much about community and tradition as they were about marking time itself. Alongside this came Fasnacht, a vibrant pre Lenten carnival that preserved much older seasonal customs. Masquerades, mummers, and playful processions filled towns with music, laughter, and satire. Masks and costumes allowed for mischief and creativity, and the rules of everyday life were happily bent before the long quiet of late winter.

description: Let the word spread far and wide, Whipping Winds is upon us! There are rustlings north of the border!! A voice on the wind calls “we’re not dead yet, eh!” Travel to the Northern Realms for the last celebration of the summer season! Join the Shire of Windegate at Williamson Park in Shelby Montana and celebrate in jubilant Northern style as Hordes from Avacal cross the border once again to celebrate our friendship. We hope! Fighting, Archery, Thrown Weapons, Dancing and Music, Arts and Classes, and Shopping! All are to be found in abundant supply amongst the trees along the shore of the Marias River. Before we batten down the hatches for the long nights of winter, the Kingdoms of Artemisia and Avacal shall join together on the fields of battle, and around the campfires beneath the stars, to solidify our mutual respect and kinship. The Autocrat team is planning activities for full days of merriment and contests! There will be Armored battles, on the main field, and into the woods! Don’t forget our Founder's Battle, and Sir Terrell’s booty tournament. Rapier will also have battle scenes and tournaments to determine who is the best. For the Arts & Sciences minded persons, we are planning to have classes, and display for your projects. Archery is a mainstay at this event, and there will be animal targets, Royal Rounds, and three archery championships. There will be organized children activities, and hopefully a practice of Youth Combat! Both Friday and Saturday nights, we will be hosting Haflas and Games for all to enjoy! SITE: Williamson Park, {72 Williamson Park Road, Shelby MT 59474} Gate opens Thursday at 12:00 noon, August 13th and closes Sunday at 12:00 noon, August 16th. The site is south of Shelby Montana, on the Marias River. At this time of year, the Marias is a wonderfully slow-moving river that has room for wading & swimming. Parents are asked to keep a mindful eye on their children. There are shade trees, an area for RV’s, a permanent playground, and a permanent building for toilets & fresh water. Fire restrictions will be dependent on Seasonal USFS restrictions. Pets allowed, on leash. FEES: Adults {age 18 years +} event registration fee for the weekend: $35.00 USD. Adult member registration for the weekend: $25.00 USD Children, age 17 and younger are guests of the shire. Day trip fees for Friday or Saturday $25 each day; Membership registration $15.00 each day. Make checks payable to Shire of Windegate DIRECTIONS: Take your best route on I-15 to Shelby Montana. Take exit 358 and follow the road south 1 mile to Williamson Park Road. Turn left {east). This will be a dirt road. Signs will be posted to guide travelers. If you cross the river, you have gone too far. Shelby is 7 miles north of the site, and has groceries, gas, hotels and other necessities.
